Congressman Case’s bill highlights a real problem: Hawaii’s healthcare system is buckling under federal mismanagement. The UHERO report confirms Medicare reimbursements set at national rates ignore Hawaii’s 13% higher cost of living and geographic isolation, directly causing provider shortages. But throwing more cash into broken systems won’t fix structural failures.

Case’s own press release brags about securing $12B for CDBG-DR programs—yet Lahaina still struggles with delayed recovery funds and bureaucratic gridlock. Real solutions require dismantling D.C.’s one-size-fits-all approach, auditing every dollar sent to Hawaii, and forcing agencies to align pay with local realities instead of subsidizing inefficiency.

Until Washington stops treating Hawaii as a budget afterthought, no amount of Band-Aid bills will heal this wound.
